chapter: Wartime South and the Ernie Fields band
title: Meeting Charlie Parker in Detroit and Lakeland
summary: He first met Parker in Detroit with McShann, Ben Webster raved about his 'Cherokee', and Parker had memorized the Eckstine book.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: I had met Charlie Parker before then, in Detroit, when he came through there with Jay McShann. I met him down on St. Antoine one night, and we went up to the Studio Club, because Freddie Webster and a bunch of them was playing up there, you know. And previous to that, Ben Webster came through with Duke Ellington, and he had been listening to Charlie Parker lately, and he was very impressed. And he came down to the club and he sat down and played piano with us, and he said, "You haven't heard anything until you hear Charlie Parker play 'Cherokee'" -- you know, the Ray Noble composition. He said, "You've got to hear him play 'Cherokee.'" Boy, he was raving about Charlie Parker playing "Cherokee."
This was in 1942. Well, I had heard Charlie at the theatre also with McShann, but I hadn't really heard him play when he could really stretch, you know. And I had
listened to him on the records with McShann. I remember his "Sepian Bounce" was a classic solo. [SINGS IT] On and on... It was beautiful!

And this particular night, when they played in Lakeland, Florida, they had only been together four days. And Charlie Parker was sitting on the book. He had memorized the book! [LAUGHS] Yeah...! He was just sitting there staring out in space and playing everything, playing all the lead, everything, you know. It was just fantastic.
